A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same GaussianDWM work. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v1 contains supplementary Sections A-E; these are absent from the complete supplied v3 PDF, rather than inaccessible through extraction.

before.justification: v1 reports original GaussianDWM results on NuInteract, nuScenes and OmniDrive, including quantitative comparisons, ablations and qualitative generation examples.

after.justification: v3 reports original NuInteract understanding and nuScenes generation results, including component ablations in Tables 1-4 and qualitative results in Figures 3-4.

M1.justification: v3 replaces cross-attention terminology with similarity calculation in the sampling description and Table 2. Figure 2 also replaces top-k with k-means, although Section 3.2 and Table 2 retain top-k. Without operational definitions resolving these inconsistencies, a substantive sampler change cannot reliably be distinguished from relabeling or correction. The principal architecture and main losses remain.

E1.justification: Reported coverage contracts through removal of the OmniDrive scene-understanding evaluation in v1 Appendix E/Table 6 and the explicit rainy/nighttime understanding and generation cases in Figures 7-8. NuInteract, nuScenes and their main tasks remain. These omissions establish reduced documented evaluation coverage, not exclusion of those weather conditions from the retained training data.

E2.justification: Removing v1 Table 6 eliminates the evaluated comparisons with GPT-4o, LLaVA-OV, OmniDrive, OmniDrive-2D, OmniDrive-BEV, Separated unification and HERMES. This includes the direct comparison with the closest related unified model. Comparator membership in the retained main benchmark tables and Figure 4 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 revises the stated alignment policy from training sparsifier/transformer modules with the backbone/tokenizer frozen to freezing the entire VLM and training the aligner. The supplementary token-budget sweep and 30-scene controlled evaluation also disappear. Retained benchmark metrics, six-camera inputs, frame-rate interpolation and generation resolutions remain unchanged. Newly stated 5k/30k training steps do not establish increased budgets or reruns.

E4.justification: v3 removes token-count sensitivity at 128, 512 and 4096 tokens (Table 5), the separate world-knowledge/Gaussian ablation (Table 7), its qualitative inspection (Figure 5), and additional cases including rain and nighttime (Figures 6-8). Main component and dual-condition ablations remain, with Table 2 now describing similarity-based sampling.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experimental results. References to significant improvements are qualitative claims, not statistical testing.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes GaussianDWM BLEU from 66.17 to 68.78, planning accuracy from 66.27 to 80.95, and average score from 57.14 to 59.23; its grounding scores remain unchanged. Table 2 updates and fills additional entries. Supplementary Tables 5-7 and Figures 5-8 disappear, while Tables 3-4 retain their values. The revised scores do not establish controlled performance gains given the unresolved sampling and training changes.

T1.justification: Removing Appendix B deletes the explicit autoencoder reconstruction and language-feature learning objectives in Equations 9-10. Main Equations 1-5 remain unchanged, and neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs. This is a loss of formal specification, not evidence that the underlying auxiliary losses were abandoned.

C1.justification: The central claims of a unified 3D-Gaussian understanding/generation framework remain unchanged. The performance claim is narrowed from state-of-the-art results across all four tasks to state-of-the-art average performance in Table 1 and accompanying text. Section 4.3 additionally states a 13.6% relative average-score advantage.

C2.justification: The removed supplement contained interpretations about efficient information retention with fewer tokens, increasing benefits of world knowledge under larger viewpoint shifts, and robustness in rain/night conditions. Appendix C's explanation of why token-level language conditioning preserves useful semantic structure also disappears. The main semantic/spatial-coherence interpretation remains, without new substantive limitations.

D1.justification: v3 loses detailed reconstruction/filtering instructions, trajectory-QA construction and coordinate conventions, sample JSON formats, Gaussian loading rules, trainable-parameter fractions, and the CLIP/type-embedding conditioning pathway from Appendices B-C. It adds explicit 5k alignment and 30k LoRA steps. Hardware, generation resolutions and the code-release promise remain, but the net loss of reproducibility information is substantial.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly credits UniFuture alongside HERMES as preceding unified understanding/generation models and expands supporting citations, including 3D-LLM, 3D-VLA and RayNova. GPT-4 and OmniDrive references disappear with the supplementary comparison. The related-work organization and central distinction based on language-aligned 3D Gaussians remain.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section order are retained, but removing supplementary Sections A-E substantially abridges the document's explanatory structure, including worked data formats and extended implementation discussion. v3 also rewrites the alignment-training and predecessor-positioning passages and adds acknowledgements.

P2.justification: v3 removes three supplementary tables and four figures rather than relocating them. Figure 2 is revised with different sampling labels, AE terminology and abbreviated trajectory examples. Table 2 gains a fully populated, highlighted final row, and the main-text layout is compacted. Figures 3-4 retain their visual examples.

improvement.justification: v3 improves average-performance wording and discloses training-step counts, but removes the direct HERMES/OmniDrive comparison, important sampling and conditioning ablations, adverse-condition examples, and extensive reproduction instructions. These losses substantially weaken verification of the central contributions. The new Figure 2 k-means versus text/Table 2 top-k inconsistency further reduces methodological clarity; the higher reported scores do not compensate for these deficiencies.
